transcript:
Meeting Header: Date/Time: 2025-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 mins | Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Rivera (CTO - Verdant), Samir Gupta (ML Eng), Priya Menon (Product)

Summary:
- Initial discovery focused on model selection for a mix of multilingual customer support and long-context document summarization.
- Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Need for tool/function calling and 100k+ context for long docs is a potential blocker; discussion around available open models and quantization options.

Topics:
- Context window requirements (50k vs 100k vs 256k)
- Multilingual coverage (EN, ES, FR, JA, ZH)
- Tool-calling/function-calling support and LLM orchestration
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (security, KMS, audit logs)
- Benchmarking next steps and POC timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Laura from Redwood, AE on this account. Marcus our solutions engineer is here as well. \n[00:08] Ellen Rivera: Hi Laura, thanks. I think we'll get started, we have about 45 minutes. I'll let Samir and Priya intro themselves.
[00:13] Samir Gupta: Hey all, Samir, ML engineer at Verdant. We're evaluating model choices for two main workloads: multilingual customer support routing + extraction, and really long-form contract summarization.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Priya here, product. High level: accuracy needs to be enterprise-grade, latency under 1s for short chats, and we also want to automate parts of workflows via tool calls.
[00:30] Marcus Patel: Great, thanks. Quick Q to start — what are your current stack and constraints? Are you running anything in-house now?
[00:37] Ellen Rivera: We're currently using a mix — some internal models for embeddings and a hosted provider for chat, but costs spiked. Data residency and auditability are big for us because we're in fintech-ish verticals. Also curious about long context windows for contract summarization, we're talking tens of thousands of tokens, maybe 100k in some cases.
[00:52] Laura Chen: Good context. Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicate — sorry, Dedicated — and Private deployments. For 100k+ contexts we typically look at Dedicated or Private with models that have extended context training or specialized kernels; we can also do prefix-KV caching for repeated sections.
[01:06] Samir Gupta: Can you run through model recommendations? We prefer open models — lower vendor lock-in.
[01:11] Marcus Patel: Sure. For open-models, common choices are: Mistral and derivatives for 7- to 8B instruction-tuned options, Llama2-family (Llama 2 70B variants) if you need higher capability, Falcon 40B for many instruction tasks, and some of the newer long-context variants — there are 32k, 65k and community-ported 128k variants. Redwood maintains performance profiles in our model catalog so we can show you latency and cost tradeoffs per model and per infra.
[01:37] Priya Menon: Multilingual support is important. Which models give us decent Japanese/Chinese?
[01:42] Marcus Patel: Llama2-70B and some Mistral fine-tuned variants do OK, but for East Asian languages some community models or specialized multilingual models perform better. We can surface evaluation scores per language — Redwood Optimize can run micro-evals on your prompt set.
[01:55] Ellen Rivera: About function/tool calling — we need the model to call external adapters to do things like database lookups, run scrapers, or call internal microservices. How does that work?
[02:03] Laura Chen: Redwood supports structured tool/function calling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we wrap calls through the API and handle streaming and function payloads. On Dedicated/Private you can host connectors inside your VPC, and the model runtime supports tool invocation hooks. There may be small latency tradeoffs but you get tighter control on security.
[02:20] Samir Gupta: Latency numbers? We're targeting <1s median for chat, but for longer summarization it's okay to be a few seconds.
[02:27] Marcus Patel: On Hosted with a 13B-ish model you can often get sub-500ms token latency for short contexts; with batching and larger models latency increases. Dedicated provides predictable throughput and lower variance; Private gives you control but depends on your infra. We'll include sample p99/p50 numbers in the benchmark.
[02:42] Priya Menon: Cost is a huge factor. Any guidance on quantized performance? We're trying to justify a Dedicated pool vs Hosted consumption.
[02:49] Marcus Patel: Absolutely — quantization (int8/q4 variants) can reduce cost 2-4x with modest quality delta. Redwood's runtime supports various quant paths; we recommend testing both float16 and int8 for your prompts. Dedicated reserved capacity typically beats pay-as-you-go Hosted at sustained traffic.
[03:05] Ellen Rivera: For the long docs — 100k context — do we need a special model or can we chunk and post-process?
[03:12] Marcus Patel: You can chunk + retrieval/overlap, often cheaper. For cases where you want the model to reason across the whole doc we recommend either models built for long context or kernel/compilation options that support long KV caches. There are community 100k+ context variants, but they're more experimental. For production we'd propose a Dedicated set up with a long-context model or a hybrid: an embedding+retrieval layer with chunked prompts and followed by a shorter final prompt to synthesize.
[03:35] Samir Gupta: Any caveats with tool-calling + long context?
[03:39] Marcus Patel: Tool-calling is orthogonal, but orchestration is key. You want deterministic function signatures; we support function schemas. Long context increases memory usage, so we size the Dedicated GPUs accordingly.
[03:49] Priya Menon: Security: SSO / SAML, audit logs, KMS — our security team will need those docs.
[03:55] Laura Chen: We'll send the security pack — SOC 2 Type II report, ISO notes, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML/SCIM docs, and audit log examples. Private deployments can have customer-managed KMS and no egress to Redwood control plane if needed.
[04:06] Ellen Rivera: Are there enterprise references in fintech?
[04:09] Laura Chen: Yes, we have customers in regulated industries; I'll include anonymized references and case studies.
[04:16] Samir Gupta: About multilingual evals — can you run our prompts?
[04:19] Marcus Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run targeted micro-evals on your prompt set across candidate models and quant settings; we typically run a 100-300 prompt sample to get comparative metrics.
[04:29] Priya Menon: We sometimes need tool calling to maintain session state and then call internal billing APIs, that must be secure. Will Redwood Dedicated keep logs locally?
[04:36] Marcus Patel: Dedicated can be configured so logs are sent to your SIEM or retained in your VPC; Private gives the most isolation. We also support token-level redaction in transit and at rest.
[04:46] Ellen Rivera: What's the rough plan and timeline for a POC? We want to move quickly, ideally 3 weeks to a pilot.
[04:52] Laura Chen: Typical POC cadence: week 0 — align and get access to sample prompts/data; week 1 — run bench + micro-evals; week 2 — tune quant / batching and run integration tests (tool calls); week 3 — initial results + next steps. We can compress if you have internal bandwidth.
[05:07] Samir Gupta: For benchmarking — what do you need from us?
[05:10] Marcus Patel: Sample prompt set, 3 representative shapes (short chat, mid-length extraction ~2-4k tokens, long doc summarization ~50k-100k or chunked), and a target concurrency. We will run latency/throughput and output-quality comparisons across 2-3 candidate models.
[05:25] Priya Menon: Any immediate model recommendation to start with?
[05:27] Marcus Patel: Start with a mid-sized instruction-tuned model (e.g., Llama2-13B variant or Mistral-instruct 7B) for quick iteration, and run a parallel test on a 70B or Falcon-40B variant for quality baseline. For the long-context POC consider a 65k or community 128k variant, or use a retrieval synthesis approach.
[05:46] Ellen Rivera: About pricing — if we go Dedicated reserved capacity, are there commitments?
[05:50] Laura Chen: Yes Dedicated is usually monthly/annual commits; we'll send a tiered pricing sheet — we've seen teams get to equivalent or lower unit cost at ~3-6 months of steady usage compared to Hosted.
[05:59] Samir Gupta: Offline question on embeddings — do you support dense + sparse/ANN options?
[06:03] Marcus Patel: We support vector embeddings with multiple index choices; can plug to your vector DB or host a managed index.
[06:09] Priya Menon: Ok next steps for us: share prompt sets, prioritize which workload first, and schedule the technical deep dive.
[06:16] Laura Chen: Great. We'll send the pricing + security docs and Marcus will follow up with the benchmark plan. Can we lock a tentative tech-deep-dive slot next week?
[06:24] Ellen Rivera: Week of 2025-12-08 works.
[06:28] Laura Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the deck and docs.
[06:32] Samir Gupta: Thanks.
[06:33] Priya Menon: Appreciate it.
[06:34] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional misrecognitions around model names and KV vs K-V cache terminology. Some speaker overlap around 00:30-01:00.
